issues.t: Airbag light from a failed passenger seat sensor
issues.sym: The airbag warning light stays on or flickers, a "service airbag" message or chime appears, or the passenger airbag-off light stays lit even with an adult in the seat.
issues.why: A pressure-sensing mat and module under the passenger seat cushion tell the airbag computer whether someone is sitting there. On these roadsters the mat or its wiring often bends, cracks or loses contact, so the system shuts off the passenger airbag and sets a fault. Many owners report it coming back even after the recall work.
issues.next: Treat the passenger airbag as not working until it is fixed, and keep children and small adults out of that seat. Have a shop read the airbag codes. Ask a GM dealer to check your VIN for open recall 17V-061 first, then ask about the sensor kit if the recall fix did not hold.

issues.t: Passenger airbag sensor can bend and turn the airbag off (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag may be switched off without a clear reason; you may see the airbag light or the passenger airbag-off light.
issues.why: The occupant sensor in the passenger seat can bend or get damaged and stop the front passenger airbag from deploying. GM recall 17V-061 covers these cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or with a GM dealer and have the free recall work done. If the light returns afterward, go back and ask for a further look.

issues.t: Ignition switch can slip out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine can suddenly shut off while driving, especially over bumps or if the key ring is heavy. Power steering and power brakes get much harder, and the airbags may not deploy in a crash.
issues.why: The ignition switch needs too little force to turn, so it can be bumped from Run to Accessory or Off. This is GM recall 14V-047, the large ignition switch recall; it was later widened to cars that may have received a faulty replacement switch.
issues.next: Until the recall is done, carry only the car key on the ring. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and get the free switch replacement. If the engine cuts out while moving, steer firmly to a safe stop.

issues.t: Key can come out when not in Off (recall)
issues.sym: You can pull the key out while the ignition is not fully off, and the car may not be locked in Park or in gear, so it could roll away.
issues.why: Worn or out-of-spec ignition lock cylinders let the key come out in the wrong position. GM recall 14V-171 replaces the cylinder where needed and recuts the keys.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake when you leave the car. Check your VIN for recall 14V-171 and have the free repair done.

issues.t: Rear differential pinion seal leaks (recall)
issues.sym: Gear oil drips from the front of the rear differential, sometimes onto the exhaust where it smokes or smells hot. If it runs low you may hear grinding from the rear.
issues.why: A seal supplier changed the seal material without approval, so the pinion seal can leak. If the differential loses its oil it can be damaged and, in the worst case, lock the rear wheels. GM recall 07V-589 replaces the seal.
issues.next: Look under the car for oil at the rear differential. Check your VIN for recall 07V-589. If you see a leak or hear grinding, have the fluid level checked before driving far.

issues.t: Seat mounting studs may be too weak (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign. You would not notice anything until a crash.
issues.why: Some cars were built with one to four inner seat mounting studs that were not strong enough, so the seat and belt might not hold the occupant as designed in a crash. Covered by recall 07V-454.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. The dealer inspects the studs and replaces any weak one with a bolt for free.

issues.t: Rear differential grinds, clunks or fails
issues.sym: Grinding or whining from the rear when accelerating or turning, clunks when shifting or getting on and off the gas, jerky turns, or in bad cases the rear wheels binding.
issues.why: The rear differential is a weak point on these cars, especially after leaks have let the oil run low. Limited-slip units can also bind or chatter in tight turns when the clutch packs or fluid wear.
issues.next: Have the differential oil level and condition checked right away. If you feel binding or the rear wheels skip, stop driving it and have it towed; a seized differential can cause a loss of control.

issues.t: Rear axle shaft seals seep gear oil
issues.sym: Oily film or drips on the inside of a rear wheel or under the differential.
issues.why: The seals where the axle shafts leave the differential commonly seep on these cars at any mileage. Left alone, the differential can run low on oil.
issues.next: A light seep is not an emergency, but have the seal replaced soon and the differential topped up so it does not run dry.

issues.t: Weak brakes right after start-up
issues.sym: For the first 30 to 60 seconds after a cold start or after the car has sat for hours, the brake pedal is hard and the car keeps creeping or rolls further than expected, often when backing out of a driveway.
issues.why: Some 2008 cars rely on a brake-boost strategy that needs engine vacuum or a pump to build up; right after start-up the power assist can be weak. GM told dealers this was normal operation (bulletin 07-05-22-002), though some cars got a software update.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Press the brake firmly and give the car a minute after a cold start before moving. Because this affects stopping, have a dealer or qualified brake shop check the vacuum assist, look for software updates and confirm the system works as it should.

issues.t: Convertible top leaks water into the cabin
issues.sym: Wet carpet or seats after rain or a car wash, water around the A-pillars, or wind noise from the top edges.
issues.why: The manual soft top seals against the windshield frame and body with weatherstrips that can sit out of place, and drains can clog. Poor top fit and misaligned panels behind the seats are common.
issues.next: Dry the interior quickly to prevent mold. Ask a shop to water-test the car, reseat or replace the weatherstrips, clear the drains and adjust the top.

issues.t: Convertible top latches stick or will not release
issues.sym: The top will not unlatch at the windshield or at the rear buttress, or it will not latch firmly when closed.
issues.why: The front and rear top latches and the deck-lid latch wear or go out of adjustment over time.
issues.next: Do not force the top. Have the latches lubricated and adjusted, or replaced if broken.

issues.t: Trunk lid bent or out of line
issues.sym: The rear deck lid sits unevenly, gaps look wrong, or the panel behind the seats is cracked.
issues.why: Closing the trunk while the top is only partly folded can bend the lid, and the complicated top movement can push panels out of line.
issues.next: Always finish lowering or raising the top before shutting the trunk. A body shop can usually realign a tweaked lid.

issues.t: Blower fan quits as the resistor connector melts
issues.sym: The fan stops on some or all speeds, you smell hot plastic, or see smoke from under the passenger side of the dash.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor and its wiring connector can overheat and melt. Owners note the same parts are shared with the Hummer H3, which had a recall for it; these cars did not.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Have the resistor and connector replaced together with the updated parts.

issues.t: Reduced power from a failing high-pressure fuel pump
issues.sym: Check engine light with fuel pressure codes such as P0087, P0089 or P2188, reduced-power mode, hesitation, or an engine that starts and then stalls.
issues.why: The direct-injection 2.0L turbo uses an engine-driven high-pressure fuel pump. When it wears out it cannot hold rail pressure, so the computer limits power.
issues.next: Avoid hard driving and get the codes read. A shop should check fuel rail pressure before replacing parts; the pump is a common fix.

issues.t: Camshaft timing codes from actuators or a stretched chain
issues.sym: Check engine light with codes such as P0011 or P0016, rough idle, or a rattle at start-up.
issues.why: The variable cam timing actuators or their solenoids can fail. At high mileage the timing chain, tensioner and guides can stretch and throw off cam timing.
issues.next: Check the oil level and have the codes read soon. Ignoring a stretched chain can lead to engine damage.

issues.t: Overheating from a failed cooling fan or thermostat
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, the coolant light comes on, or steam and coolant smell come from under the hood.
issues.why: Owners report the radiator fan quitting, thermostats sticking, and at least one radiator hose blowing off.
issues.next: Pull over and shut the engine off if the gauge goes into the red. Do not open a hot radiator cap. Have the fan, thermostat and hoses checked before driving again.

issues.t: Water pump leak on the 2.0L turbo
issues.sym: Coolant drips or a sweet smell near the front of the engine, and the coolant level keeps dropping.
issues.why: The water pump wears out, and on the turbo engine it sits under the turbocharger, so it takes a lot of labor to reach.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up and watch the gauge. Have the pump replaced before it fails completely and overheats the engine.

issues.t: Parking brake will not hold
issues.sym: The car rolls on a slope with the parking brake on, or the lever goes up too far.
issues.why: The parking brake cable can stretch or go out of adjustment, and the rear calipers that apply it can stick.
issues.next: Use Park or first gear and wheel chocks on hills until it is fixed. Have the cable adjusted or the rear caliper serviced.

issues.t: Air conditioning stops cooling
issues.sym: Warm air from the vents, A/C that cycles on and off, or a whining noise and refrigerant smell.
issues.why: Owners report failed compressors, condensers and A/C hoses.
issues.next: Have the system checked for leaks before simply recharging it.

issues.t: Check engine light from the gas cap
issues.sym: A steady check engine light with no change in how the car drives.
issues.why: A loose, worn or cracked gas cap lets fuel vapor escape, which the evaporative emissions system reports as a leak.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks. If the light stays on after a few days of driving, replace the cap and have the code read.

issues.t: Shock absorbers leak
issues.sym: Oil residue on the shocks, a bouncy or floaty ride, or less grip in corners.
issues.why: Shocks on these cars can start leaking even at low mileage.
issues.next: Have the shocks inspected with the wheels off. Replace leaking ones in pairs and use the right parts for your suspension package.

issues.t: Brittle cupholders and console trim break
issues.sym: Cupholders jam or crack, the center armrest cracks, or interior clips and panels rattle.
issues.why: The interior uses hard, brittle plastics that crack under light pressure and clips that break with age.
issues.next: This is a nuisance, not a safety issue. Used or aftermarket trim parts are the usual fix.

issues.t: Fiberglass front fender panels crack
issues.sym: Cracks or breaks in the front fender panels behind the front wheels.
issues.why: The Sky uses fiberglass panels there that crack from road debris or if the car is lifted or jacked in the wrong spot.
issues.next: Ask any shop to use the correct lift points. Cracked panels can be repaired or replaced by a body shop.

issues.t: Water in the trunk
issues.sym: Damp carpet or standing water in the trunk after rain.
issues.why: Water can enter around the tail light and bumper mounting screws, and the top and deck lid seals can let water past.
issues.next: Have the tail light and bumper screw holes sealed and the deck lid seal checked.

issues.t: Dead battery leaves keys and tire sensors unprogrammed
issues.sym: The car will not start after sitting, and after a jump the key fobs or tire pressure sensors may stop working.
issues.why: A roadster that sits for long stretches drains its battery. After a long dead-battery period one owner needed a bulletin reprogram of the engine computer to relearn the fobs and tire sensors.
issues.next: Use a battery maintainer if the car sits for weeks. If fobs or TPMS stop working after a dead battery, ask a dealer about the reprogramming bulletin.

issues.t: Ticking noise from the direct injectors
issues.sym: A steady clicking or ticking from the top of the engine, most noticeable at idle.
issues.why: Direct fuel injectors on the 2.0L turbo fire at very high pressure and make a ticking sound that can be mistaken for a valve problem.
issues.next: If the engine runs well and the check engine light is off, this is usually normal. Have it checked if the noise changes or a warning light comes on.

issues.t: Sticking brake caliper slides
issues.sym: Brakes drag, grind or wear unevenly.
issues.why: One owner found the caliper slide pins were never greased at the factory and had stuck by 5,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the slide pins cleaned and greased at the next brake service.
